subject: CS Implementation: model candidates, context constraints, and token-traffic estimate

Subject: CS kickoff — need context/volume so we can pick candidates

Hi Marta / Alex —

Thanks for agreeing to jump into onboarding planning. Before our technical kickoff next week we want to capture the core constraints so we can target the right model family and a realistic token-volume forecast. I put a short list of questions below — a couple can be filled in by Alex if it's more ops-focused.

Quick asks (if you could reply inline):
- Primary feature(s) you plan to enable in month 1 (e.g., triage summarization, chat support, clinical note extraction)
- Typical context per request: average input chars or tokens, and maximum context required (is 8k enough, or do you need 32k+?)
- Expected user/base volume: concurrent users or daily active users, and rough average requests per user per day
- SLA/latency expectations (p95 generation latency target) and any compliance constraints beyond HIPAA (e.g., data residency)

I'll loop in Dev and Stephanie for a first-pass model candidate shortlist and a token-traffic estimate once we have these. Attaching a simple token-profile template — please fill the green cells with your numbers.

Attachments: ceres_token_profile_v1.xlsx

Thanks,
Hannah

Hi Hannah —

Thanks — quick answers below, filled the token-profile spreadsheet and reattached.

- Primary features: patient message triage (priority detection + short summary) and physician note auto-draft (structured output: problem list + plan bullets).
- Typical context: inbound messages average ~650 characters (~120 tokens). For note auto-draft the context will include the patient’s last 2 notes + current intake (~4,500 chars, ~820 tokens). Peak requirement: up to 8,000 tokens per request (we have some long visit bundles).
- Volume: pilot cohort ~150 clinicians, average 8 requests/clinician/day (triage + draft). For pilot month expect ~1,200 requests/day. Target production scales to 8k clinicians over 12 months; that would be ~64k requests/day at steady state.
- SLA & compliance: p95 latency target for triage <400ms, for draft <1.2s. All PHI must stay in US regions; we need SOC2 attestation and an indication that logs can be retained for 90 days.

Let us know if you need breakdown by interactive vs. batch.

— Marta
Marta Lopez
Dir. Product Ops, Ceres Health
marta@cereshealth.com

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: CS kickoff — need context/volume so we can pick candidates

Thanks Marta — this is really helpful. Based on the profile I sketched a candidate short-list and a first-pass token/throughput estimate (see bullets). I prioritized models that balance latency and cost and that we already have performance profiles for in US regions.

Model candidate shortlist (pilot):
- small-llm-v1 (quantized 8-bit): good for triage classification & short summaries. Expected generation tokens per request ~60, p95 latency ~180-300ms with 1-2 token streaming.
- med-instr-7B (FP16): better for structured draft outputs (plan bullets). Expected generation tokens per request ~220, p95 latency ~600-900ms.
- long-context-13B (Q4_0): for edge cases when you need ~8k context; higher latency/cost, keep as fallback for large bundles.

Token traffic (pilot ~1,200 req/day):
- Triage (~1 request per user/day): input ~120 tokens, output ~60 tokens => ~180 tokens/request => ~216k tokens/day
- Draft (~1 request per user/day): input ~820 tokens, output ~220 tokens => ~1,040 tokens/request => ~1.25M tokens/day
- Combined pilot estimate: ~1.47M tokens/day (~44M tokens/month)

Production projection (64k req/day steady state):
- Using same proportions: ~78M tokens/day => ~2.34B tokens/month.

Operational notes / tradeoffs:
- We recommend using small-llm-v1 as default route for triage to meet the <400ms target; med-instr-7B for draft. For >6k token contexts route to long-context-13B as fallback with explicit user consent for longer processing times.
- Caching: prefix caching on patient history (KV cache) can reduce effective context reads for note drafting in many cases — worth instrumenting in pilot.
- Autoscaling: pilot can run on a small Dedicated pool; for production we'll need reserved capacity with burst to handle daily peaks.

I've attached sizing_notes_20260821.md with the math and assumptions. Happy to walk through in the kickoff.

— Dev

Dev — thanks for the breakdown. Two quick ops questions:
1) For the production projection you quoted ~2.34B tokens/month — can you confirm that assumes retention of all logs/token data for 90 days? If not, what changes?
2) What kind of latency headroom do we need on Dedicated capacity to hit p95 <400ms for triage at 64k req/day — is a single GPU per X workers sufficient or do we need sharding?

Also Marta: compliance wants a SOC2 statement and a brief of the audit log retention controls before the procurement packet.

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Mon, 24 Aug 2026 10:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: CS kickoff — need context/volume so we can pick candidates

Alex / team — quick answers and next steps.

1) Retention assumption: the 2.34B tokens/month projection is independent of retention; retention affects storage cost and audit logs volume. If you retain request/response bodies for 90 days we estimate ~2.34B * average token size (approx 4 bytes/token compressed) => ~9.4GB/day of compressed token payloads (~282GB/month). We'll provide a SOC2 attestation document and sample log-retention spec (attached: redwood_implementation_checklist.pdf).

2) Latency headroom & capacity sizing: for triage using small-llm-v1 optimized on our runtime, our benchmarks show a single A10G-equivalent GPU with 12 inference workers can sustain ~12k triage/sec equivalent at p95 ~320ms (subject to batching behavior). To hit 64k requests/day (which averages ~0.74 req/sec) you'll be fine with a small cluster but need headroom for bursts: recommended Dedicated baseline = 2x A10G-equivalent GPUs with autoscale for peaks. For drafting (med-instr-7B) we recommend at least 1x A100-equivalent node dedicated during office hours for consistent latency; autoscale for weekends/peaks.

Notes:
- We will instrument prefix/KV caching to reduce redundant reads for note drafting.
- We'll limit fallback to long-context-13B for only those requests tagged with >6k tokens to reduce cost.

Next steps: Hannah to schedule kickoff (technical deep-dive), Dev to share a concise capacity runbook and Stephanie to send SOC2 + log-retention spec.

Thanks —
Stephanie Nguyen
Product Ops (Onboarding), Redwood Inference
